model.name: Leaky integrate-and-fire whole-brain model
model.reference: Shiu, P.K. et al. A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing. Nature 634, 210-219 (2024). github.com/philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model
model.sign_rule: per presynaptic neuron's predicted transmitter: GABA and glutamate inhibitory, acetylcholine and all others excitatory (Shiu et al. Connectivity_783.parquet)
model.simulator: numba re-implementation of the Brian2 update schedule of Shiu et al. model.py (exact integration)

trials.rate: mean rate over the extra trials

exact_match_test.description: Spike-for-spike comparison with Brian2 2.9.0 running Shiu et al. model.py equations/parameters on a 463-neuron sub-network (neurons active in the v630 sugar run, 22,525 connections), identical Poisson input events, 1 s at 200 Hz

olfactory_runaway_in_brian2.description: Full v783 network, 33 right ORN_DM1 neurons at 150 Hz, first 100 ms: Brian2 2.9.0 running the authors' model.py (run_exp, 1 trial) vs this simulator (4 trials). Both show the same antennal-lobe runaway.

stimulus.description: Labellar sugar-sensing gustatory receptor neurons (GRNs), both sides: the 21 + 10 neurons stimulated in Shiu et al. (Fig. 1, S1), mapped to FlyWire v783, driven at 150 Hz.
Labellar bitter GRNs (types LB1a/d, LB1b, LB1c = the Shiu et al. Fig. 3 bitter set), both sides, driven at 150 Hz.
Sugar and bitter GRNs driven together at 150 Hz each: bitter input suppresses the sugar-evoked feeding motor output (Shiu et al. Fig. 3a).

experiments.label: Smell: geosmin (DA2)

stimulus.description: Olfactory receptor neurons of glomerulus DA2 (Or56a; geosmin, the smell of mould that flies innately avoid) in the right antenna, driven at 100 Hz.

experiments.note: Driven below the default 150 Hz on purpose: in this model any olfactory receptor input of ~115-150 Hz (and DM1 input even at 15 Hz) ignites a self-sustaining runaway in the antennal lobe (excitatory local neurons) that recruits ~8,400 neurons incl. ~3,400 Kenyon cells. Every one of the 53 right-antenna ORN types except DA3 triggers it at 150 Hz, so the default-rate response is a model artefact rather than odour-specific activity.

experiments.label: Light flash

stimulus.description: A patch of 300 neighbouring R1-6 photoreceptors (about 50 ommatidia) in the right eye (non-DRA, nearest to a neuron at the eye's median position), driven at 150 Hz: a small spot of light.

experiments.note: Real photoreceptors release histamine (inhibitory onto L1/L2); the model signs synapses from the predicted transmitter (mostly acetylcholine for R1-6), so here the flash excites the lamina.

stimulus.description: Auditory Johnston's organ neurons (JO-A and JO-B subtypes, sound/near-field vibration sensors in the antenna), both antennae, driven at 150 Hz.
Johnston's organ neurons JO-C/E, JO-F and JO-D/m of one antenna (the Shiu et al. Fig. 5 set, mapped to v783) that trigger antennal grooming, driven at 150 Hz.
Right-side LC4 and LPLC2 visual projection neurons (looming detectors), driven at 150 Hz; they converge on the Giant Fiber descending neuron (DNp01).
